key_insight: A temporal machine learning time-to-event framework can personalize predictions of ALS functional decline and wheelchair-free survival by combining longitudinal ALSFRS-R trajectories with survival modeling.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians and care teams anticipate assistive device needs earlier, support proactive care planning, and improve trial stratification for ALS.
method: Built a harmonized longitudinal ALS dataset from diagnosis, ALSFRS-R, daily living, and demographic records.
Clustered ALSFRS-R items into functional domains and modeled nonlinear decline with generalized additive mixed models.
Used temporal ML plus Cox survival modeling to generate individualized survival curves and predict wheelchair access timing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports integrated longitudinal cohort data and modeling across multiple functional domains, with lower limb measures emerging as the strongest predictors of earlier wheelchair access.
watch_item: Performance, external validation, and real-world deployment details are not provided in the abstract, so generalizability and calibration need confirmation.
paper_title: A Temporal Machine Learning-Based Time-to-Event Model for Predicting ALS Progression and Healthcare Utilization
